analyses.summary: Data warning first: audit/mute/ and audit/framecheck/ are no longer in the working tree. A `reset: moving to HEAD` ran at 2026-10-16 19:25:42 (reflog). The only remaining copy is the untracked parent of stash@{0} (19:06:48, commit 6211daa): 6,146 mute files (6.08 GB) and 557 framecheck files, plus untracked books/<slug>/ files for 48 books. If that stash is dropped, all of it is lost. I read it read-only via git archive into the scratchpad. Coverage: 24 Antidote books with mute runs, latest run each (720 frames, 35 WRONG, 55 dead), plus fc1 for burn-of-the-everflame (262 beats, 13 WRONG, 68 dead). I skipped 1 book (wonder: art.json 11:53 is newer than run3 11:27) and the 9 Vox books. Combined and de-duplicated, that is 149 failure items: 46 WRONG and 119 dead. Ownership of WRONG: ENGINE 21 (46%), AUTHORING 13 (28%), VOCABULARY 6 (13%), RATER 6 (13%). Ownership of dead: AUTHORING 76 (64%), ENGINE 30 (25%), VOCABULARY 11 (9%). Burn is not representative. Its art.json leaves cast unauthored on 113 of 262 beats, and that produces almost all twin, silhouette and engine-filled failures. In the 23 other books, dead is 85% authoring (41/48), and the largest class is bare-figure-no-object (35/48 dead). 59% of judged frames have no icon at all (425/720). Those frames are dead at 9.4% vs 5.1% with an icon, and WRONG at 5.9% vs 3.4%. Outside burn, the largest WRONG class is strike-negation-misread (9 of 29). Engine fixes that apply across books: (1) The neutral mouth is still v1, a U-curve, in Everyman.tsx:52-61. Neutral faces read as smiling 19% of the time overall, 49% with stubble vs 11% clean-shaven. (2) The `game` icon draws a trophy cup: 3/3 WRONG in burn, and it appears in 44 scenes across 19 books. (3) The authorship lock seals the engine's twin cast whenever art.json sets only `set` (plan-antidote.js:1183). (4) Strike text fails as negation grammar: the struck part is misread, or the strike is not seen at all. Rater noise is real. The paired sample (burn run5 vs fc1, same 30 beats) agrees on correctness 19/30 and on only 1 of run5's 6 WRONG. 6 of the 46 WRONG are judge verdicts that contradict their own inputs. The earlier claim that silhouette frames are mostly dead is not supported: in fc1, all-silhouette frames are dead at 16% (9/55) vs 28.5% for the rest.

findings.evidence: Latest-run totals: 720 frames, 35 WRONG (4.9%), 55 dead (7.6%). fc1: 262 beats, 13 WRONG (5.0%), 68 dead (26.0%). Skipped: wonder run3 (art.json 2026-10-07T11:53 > judge 11:27). findings.impact: Engine-fixable once in code: 46% of WRONG and 25% of dead overall. If strike is counted as AUTHORING (the author picks the strike style), engine WRONG falls to 12/46 (26%).

findings.claim: Burn is an outlier. Its art.json leaves cast unauthored on 113/262 beats, and that alone produces the twin, engine-silhouette and engine-filled classes. In the other 23 books, dead is 85% authoring and mostly a figure with no object.
findings.evidence: Unauthored cast per book (snapshot): burn 113, a-good-man (published, old) 267, flowers 31, under-the-dome 30, beloved 14, all analysed recent books 0-5. Burn art.json fields: cast 142/263, expression 194/263. Mute latest runs without burn: 29 WRONG, 48 dead. Dead owners: AUTHORING 41, ENGINE 4, VOCABULARY 2, RATER 1. bare-figure-no-object = 35/48. the-art-of-saying-no run3: 9/9 dead frames have no icon (scenes 12, 29, 60, 127, 151, 159, 196, 198, 207). Base rates over 720 latest-run frames: no-icon frames n=425 (59%), dead 9.4% / WRONG 5.9%; icon frames n=295, dead 5.1% / WRONG 3.4%. fc1: no-icon dead 37.8% vs icon 21.3%.
findings.impact: Engine fixes for twins and silhouettes will move burn but barely touch the other books. There the dead budget (bar ≤5/30) is mostly spent on bare figures (35 of the 48 dead).

findings.claim: Face-reads-wrong-mood is mostly the engine's neutral mouth, and stubble makes it worse. The v2 flat mouth exists in code but was never switched on.
findings.evidence: src/engines/antidote/characters/Everyman.tsx:52-61: `NEUTRAL_MOUTH_PATHS v1 'M176,214 Q200,220 224,214'` (a U-curve, a faint smile, as the code comment says, citing Beloved scene-208) and `NEUTRAL_MOUTH_VERSION = 'v1'`. wardrobe.tsx:126 draws stubble with an upward inner arc ending under the mouth. Across all Antidote mute runs + fc1, frames with one visible non-silhouette person read as smiling at these rates: neutral 93/502 (19%), happy 75%, smirk 64%, worried 7%, sad 5%, angry 6%, blank 6%. Neutral by beard: stubble 47/96 (49%), none 44/385 (11%), full 2/11. In fc1, luther (stubble) neutral reads smiling 18/26. Examples: burn fc1 scene-13 ('smiling horned character' over 'slaughter every descended'), the-hate-u-give run3 scene-54 (officer115 neutral read as a 'smiling police officer' at a fatal stop), burn run5 scene-98 ('smiling oddly' over 'an absolute disaster'), the-hate-u-give run3 scene-07 (worried + neutral read as 'both smiling gently' over 'FAIL TO PROTECT BLACK LIVES').
findings.impact: 7 of 46 WRONG (15%) are engine-owned face misreads, 3 of them outside burn (hate-u-give). Neutral-only frames are WRONG 8.7% vs 3.5% for other frames (latest runs), and 10.0% vs 3.5% in fc1.

findings.claim: Strike-negation misread is the largest WRONG class outside burn. Viewers either read the struck phrase as the claim, read a partial strike backwards, or do not see the strike at all.
findings.evidence: 9 WRONG across 6 books, all with texts[].style='strike': skin-in-the-game run1 scene-258; the-art-of-saying-no run3 scene-36 and scene-207 (the strike was never mentioned; the viewer read 'guilt disappears quickly'); the-courage-to-be-disliked run1 scene-247; the-hate-u-give run3 scene-26 (strike not seen; 'cafeteria politics' taken as the claim); the-miracle-of-mindfulness run3 scenes 32 (partial strike 'SUE WAKES UP' read as 'Sue wakes up easily'), 48 and 94; the-second-mountain run3 scene-145. Base rate over latest runs: strike frames n=81, WRONG 9.9% vs 4.2% for non-strike. All runs: 15.9% vs 9.3%. Strike is the callout style of 1,012 of ~9,700 authored callouts across books.
findings.impact: 9/29 (31%) of non-burn WRONG. It is the single largest WRONG lever in fully authored books.

findings.claim: The `game` icon is drawn as a trophy cup, so every 'game' beat reads as 'winning'. This accounts for 3 of the 5 'trophy = winning' misreads in burn.
findings.evidence: src/engines/antidote/motifs.tsx:806 `const Game` draws a cup with handles on a base (registry line 3123: `game: Game`). fc1: concept game n=3, WRONG 3, dead 3, trophy named 3/3 (scenes 04 'A MASSIVE GAME OF CHESS', 33 'STRATEGIZE OUT OF A CRISIS', 34 'SABOTAGING HIS MILITARY ROLE'). Concept trophy n=5, trophy named 5/5, 1 WRONG (scene-116 'FANCY TITLES ARE WORTHLESS', an icon-polarity case). data/icon-readings.json has a trophy row ('status, a prize') but no game row. 44 scenes in 19 books use game (ready-player-one 8, skin-in-the-game 6, fahrenheit-451 3, lolita 3, ...).
findings.impact: 3/46 WRONG directly. A once-in-code fix (redraw, or alias to the trophy row) for 44 existing scene uses.

findings.claim: Twin cast: when an art beat authors no cast, the director stages a twoShot or split with the lead identity twice. The authorship lock then seals that cast as if it were authored.
findings.evidence: burn art.json beats 145, 146, 164, 165, 172, 173 author only callout/set (no cast). config _authorship.lock.cast = ['luther','luther'] (e.g. scene-164) and src='art'. beloved scene-281: lock.cast ['sethe','sethe'] ('Two nearly identical Black women'). The lock is written in scripts/plan-antidote.js:1183-1188 when `A.set` alone is present, recording out.characters identities. Twin scenes per book: burn 6, beloved 4, under-the-dome 10; all on unauthored-cast beats. In fc1, twoShot frames (n=5) are 100% dead and 2/5 WRONG (164 'two identical smiling ... A CHILD CUT HIS HAND'; 165 'friendly handshake' over 'HIGHLY TOXIC AND LETHAL').
findings.impact: 2 WRONG + 7 dead combined. Outside burn: 1 dead (beloved 281). The same lock rule also makes the gate-authorship report count engine choices as authored (src='art' on every failing scene).

findings.claim: The engine's silhouette cut-out mostly appears on unauthored-cast beats, but silhouette frames are NOT more often dead than average. The earlier 'silhouettes are mostly dead' claim is refuted.
findings.evidence: shots.ts: the illustration/diorama slots default `silhouette: true`. plan-antidote.js:879 un-silhouettes the lead only when the beat is staged (cast/expression/action/holds), so unauthored beats keep the black cut-out. Unauthored-silhouette scenes: burn 55, flowers 28, a-good-man 75. fc1: all-silhouette frames n=55, dead 9 (16.4%), WRONG 1, vs non-silhouette dead 28.5%. Latest mute runs: all-silhouette n=19, dead 26%. Examples: burn fc1 scene-121 ('I HAVE TO DEFEND DIEM', black silhouette + shield), scene-209, flowers run3 scene-182 (chris silhouette + book).
findings.impact: 10 dead combined (8% of dead), 9 of them engine-owned. Fixing it is cheap, but the gain is bounded, and it is concentrated in burn.

findings.claim: Generic icons that name the topic but not the claim are the second-largest dead class. About 70% of them are authoring choices (a better icon existed), and 30% are vocabulary gaps.
findings.evidence: 28 dead (AUTHORING 20, VOCABULARY 8). Examples: burn fc1 scene-09 war shield+spears for 'FORCED ALLIANCES AND BLOODLINES' (no icon exists), scene-100 target for 'FUNDED BATTALIONS' (wallet/coin/dollarExchange exist), beloved run2 scene-121 heart for 'PAUL D SHUT HIS LEDGER', the-second-mountain run3 scene-127 twoMountains for 'CLIMBED IN COMPANY' with one person shown. fc1 outcomes by concept: war n=23 dead 7, target n=6 dead 3, shield n=12 dead 4, fire n=26 dead 4.
findings.impact: 24% of dead overall, 7/48 outside burn.

findings.claim: Icon polarity: icons are drawn only in their positive, intact state, so a negated, failing or broken idea reads as its opposite.
findings.evidence: WRONG examples: burn fc1 scene-116 trophy for 'FANCY TITLES ARE WORTHLESS' (icon-readings already lists trophy neverFor 'weakness'), scene-130 intact chain for 'THIS BOND IS FAILING' (icon-readings: chains 'drawn intact'), burn run5 scene-181 heart for 'HER LOVE MADE HER MONSTROUS', the-hate-u-give run3 scene-109 home read as pride over 'respectability ... does nothing to protect'. burn fc1 scene-112: intact home over homes 'incinerated' (dead).
findings.impact: 4 WRONG + 3 dead. There is no broken or negated variant of any icon in the vocabulary.

findings.claim: Rejected-premise callouts: the authored on-screen text states the premise the narration rejects (without strike), and the viewer takes it as the message.
findings.evidence: 5 WRONG, all authoring: i-robot run1 scene-98 'THAT ROBOT LIES' (narration: robots cannot knowingly lie), flowers-in-the-attic run3 scene-30 'PURELY ON SURVIVAL INSTINCT' (narration rejects that reading), die-with-zero run3 scene-34 'NEVER CONVERT IT', the-miracle-of-mindfulness run3 scene-10 'WELLNESS APPS' (+ phone icon, read as endorsement), red-rising run2 scene-236 (already re-authored after the run). The-art-of-saying-no: readcheck (text-only) found 0 WRONG before every failing run. These items read correctly as text but wrong against the narration's stance.
findings.impact: 5/29 non-burn WRONG (17%). Together with strike, 14/29 (48%) of non-burn WRONG come from how negation and rejection are put on screen.

findings.claim: Rater noise is substantial: judges contradict their own inputs, and a single blind pass reproduces WRONG poorly.
findings.evidence: Paired sample (burn run5 vs fc1, the same 30 beats): correctness agrees 19/30, contribution 23/30, both 15/30. WRONG: run5 6, fc1 3, overlap 1. Dead: 7 vs 7, overlap 4 (scratchpad/agree.js). Explicit rater errors (6 WRONG + 2 dead): burn run5 scene-167 (the judge's why says 'Twin smiling men' but the description is a black silhouette + shield); the-miracle-of-mindfulness run3 scene-130 (its why is about 'friends murdered', i.e. it was copied from item scene-148); miracle 148 and 248 (viewer message matches the narration, yet WRONG); burn run5 scene-86 (the why says 'mostly fits fire', yet WRONG); unhinged run6 scene-44 (penalises a therapist the narration names: 'says to him in one of their sessions').
findings.impact: At least 13% of WRONG (6/46) are rater-made. On the one paired sample, 5 of 6 WRONG did not reproduce, so 30-frame WRONG counts near the ≤1 bar carry roughly ±2-3 frames of noise. This changes no bar, but any single run should be treated as a noisy sample.

findings.claim: Smaller engine defects where an authored decision does not reach the screen, or the rig draws something else.
findings.evidence: burn fc1 scene-59 (art concept heart; config props [] → blind sees 'empty forest') and scene-159 (lightbulb; props [] → 'sparse frame'). Authored concept with empty props and no diagram: burn 3, surrounded-by-idiots 13, the-paradox-of-choice 8, ready-player-one 49 (whether those render via another path is unknown). fc1 scene-162: narrator neutral+talk described as 'eyes missing'. fc1 scene-177: authored collapsed in a medium shot, 'only partly visible and cropped'. fc1 scene-195: authored flow diagram described with no labels. Vocabulary gaps (WRONG): long-way-down run2 scenes 190/191 (ghosts drawn as ordinary living people), 21-days run1 scene-177 (set 'room' drawn as a bedroom for a convenience store; no store set in schema.ts setName).
findings.impact: 6 dead + 3 WRONG. scene-59/159 break CLAUDE.md invariant 1 (an authored icon is dropped).

openQuestions: Should the operator be told right away that audit/mute and audit/framecheck exist only in stash@{0} (6211daa)? Restoring them to the working tree needs operator approval, and I am read-only.

For the 18 books whose art.json is untracked (no mtime), the snapshot config is assumed to be what was rendered. Text and scene-id agreement supports this, but changes to expression, cast or icon after a run would not be detected.
Who owns strike-negation: the engine (how a strike is drawn and placed) or authoring (choosing strike for a nuanced claim)? Engine WRONG share moves between 46% and 26% depending on the answer.

ready-player-one has 49 scenes with an authored concept and empty props, yet passed run6 (0 WRONG, 0 dead). Is concept rendered by another path in diorama shots, or are those icons silently missing? Unknown.
Rater reproducibility is measured on only one paired 30-frame sample (burn). Agreement rates on other books are unknown.
The heuristic plus manual owner split for generic-icon (AUTHORING vs VOCABULARY) is one rater's judgement (mine), not measured. A second classifier pass would give its reliability.
The 9 Vox books with mute runs were excluded, so this cause map does not cover the Vox engine.

analyses.summary: I checked all six suspected defects against the code, by looking at 7 stills, and with two scratchpad joins. The first join covers framecheck fc1 on burn-of-the-everflame: 262 frames joined with the current config. The second covers the latest mute run of each of 22 books: 660 judged frames joined with each book's current config. DATA WARNING: audit/mute, audit/framecheck, audit/candidates and the untracked books/*/config.antidote.json are no longer on disk in the main checkout. A `git stash -u` at 19:06 (stash@{0}, 'WIP on god-mode: 06d3393') swept them in, together with the .render-github-split.* state files. I read them with `git archive stash@{0}^3` into the scratchpad and did not touch the stash. Confirmed defects, largest first. (1) Beard grin: the stubble/full-beard path's upper edge is a cheek-to-cheek U just under the mouth. In burn, neutral visible faces with stubble read 'smiling' 17/31 (55%, 4 WRONG, 11 dead), against 4/29 (14%) without a beard. Across the corpus it is 7/43 vs 11/112, and 30% of cast beats (2191/7398) show a bearded face. (2) Twin cast: the planner's role-to-cast lookup maps every role the bible doesn't name to the first cast key, so the director's [protagonist, foil] becomes [luther, luther]. The staging lock then seals it whenever art.json authored only `set`. 20 beats in 3 configs (beloved 4, burn 6, under-the-dome 10), all locked. In burn fc1 all 6 twin frames are dead and 2 are WRONG. (3) Implicit silhouette: the illustration/diorama presets default to a black cut-out unless a planner sets silhouette:false, which only happens when art.json authors a cast. That hits 81 beats (burn 53, flowers 28). It is REFUTED that silhouettes are 'mostly dead': in burn they are dead 9/55 (16%, WRONG 1) vs 58/199 (29%) for frames with a visible face. In the mute corpus it is 5/17 vs 40/621, which points the other way, so the evidence is mixed. (4) Neutral mouth v1 sags into a faint smile. Neutral faces without a beard read smiling 11/112 (9.8%) vs worried 2/87 (2.3%). The flat v2 curve exists, but test-neutral-mouth.js asserts v1 stays the default. (5) Shut-eye: scene-162 was sampled exactly on a blink peak (local frame 136 + poseAt 60 = 196, which is the peak frame 2 of the 97-frame blink cycle). The rig draws no lid line, so the face shows brows with nothing under them. Corpus exposure is 15/660 frames, with 0 WRONG. (6) Poses: 'think' is an arm held straight out (read as pointing 23/94 in the corpus and 25/54 in burn, read as thinking 1/94). 'Slump' is a 10° lean (described only as standing 42/87, as slumped 4/87). Both cost few WRONG (1 each) but carry nothing. No existing test covers the beard, the twin fallback, the illustration/diorama silhouette default, or the think/slump poses.

findings.claim: The beard shape reads as a grin. Stubble and full beard draw a dark U whose upper edge runs cheek to cheek just under the mouth, so it reads as a wide smile around the real mouth line. Confirmed by looking at the frames.
findings.evidence: src/engines/antidote/wardrobe.tsx:124-136. Stubble path `M130,166 Q140,244 200,252 Q260,244 270,166 Q250,214 200,218 Q150,214 130,166 Z` at opacity 0.24; its inner (top) edge bottoms out at y≈218, while the neutral mouth (Everyman.tsx:57) spans x176-224 at y214-217. The full beard has the same inner U (Q252,220 200,222). The color is darken(hair,0.85) (Everyman.tsx:223), so dark hair gives a near-black band. The beard is drawn at Everyman.tsx:371, before the mouth (Everyman.tsx:438-440). Stills: scene-03-f1200 (judged WRONG, 'smiling man and heart'), scene-164-f44834 (twins 'smiling'), scene-10 (worried mouth inside the U) under scratchpad/stash/audit/framecheck/burn-of-the-everflame/fc1/stills/burn-of-the-everflame/. Burn fc1, visible single-mood faces: neutral+stubble read smiling 17/31 (55%), 4 WRONG, 11 dead; neutral without beard 4/29 (14%); worried+stubble read smiling 4/37. Latest mute run per book (22 books, 660 frames): neutral+stubble 7/43 (16%), neutral+full 2/9, neutral without beard 11/112 (9.8%).
findings.impact: Burn: 4 of the 13 framecheck WRONG frames (31%) and 11 of the 68 dead frames. Across the corpus it touches 2191 of the 7398 cast beats (30%) in 29 configs. Smallest fix: move the inner edge of the stubble and full beard below the mouth and flatten it (e.g. top edge from (140,200) through (200,236) to (260,200)), so the band's border never continues the mouth's corners. Optionally drop stubble contrast (opacity ~0.12, or color darken(skin) instead of darken(hair)). Verify on a cast sheet blind before shipping. No test covers it: test-neutral-mouth.js checks only the mouth.

findings.claim: Unauthored two-person shots are filled with the same identity twice, then sealed as if the author chose it. The cause is the role-to-cast lookup's fallback, not the director.
findings.evidence: The director deliberately picks two different roles (scripts/lib/antidote-director.js castRoles, 'never the same role twice', e.g. [protagonist, foil]; castCount=2 for twoShot/split/overShoulder at line 1166). plan-antidote.js:295-302 roleIndex: a role not found in the bible falls back to `byRole.narrator || Object.keys(cast)[0]`. Burn's bible roles are prose ('Diem's devoted mate…'), so both protagonist and foil resolve to `luther`. plan-antidote.js:774-804 builds the characters. The art block at 814-852 fixes the cast only when `a.cast` is authored, and those beats have none: art.json beats 145/146/164/165/172/173 author only `set`. The lock at plan-antidote.js:1183-1195 fires on `A.set` alone and stores `cast: out.characters.map(identity)`, so _authorship.lock.cast = ['luther','luther'] (verified in burn config scene-146). Stills: burn scene-164-f44834; beloved run2 img-22 (scene-281, sethe/sethe).
findings.impact: 20 beats in 3 configs (beloved 4, burn 6, under-the-dome 10), all 20 locked. Burn fc1: 6 frames, 6 dead, 2 WRONG (15% of its WRONG). Mute corpus: 2 frames (beloved run2 scene-281 dead). Smallest fix, two parts. (a) After castKeyFor, give slot n>0 the next unused cast key; if none is left, drop the shot to medium with one person. (b) At line 1183, put `cast` in the lock only when `Array.isArray(A.cast)`, otherwise record null so engine casting is not frozen as authored. The authorship-gate tests do not cover this: test-authorship-gate.js locks use cast: []. No test covers roleIndex.

findings.claim: The illustration and diorama shots draw their figure as a black cut-out by default, without any flag in the config. Planners turn it off only when art.json authors a cast. The claim that silhouette frames are mostly dead is refuted for burn; the cross-book evidence is mixed.
findings.evidence: src/engines/antidote/shots.ts:153,155 (illustration) and 164,166 (diorama) set the last argument `silhouette` to true. stageChar at shots.ts:233 uses `spec.silhouette ?? slot.silhouette`. Scene.tsx:69-78 renders a silhouetted figure through `filter: brightness(0)`. Only plan-antidote.js:849 sets silhouette:false, inside the authored-cast branch. Burn: 53 illustration/diorama beats (scenes 121-238) have characters with no silhouette field and art.json without cast (e.g. art[121] = {set:'stage'}). Still scene-121-f33316 shows a solid black horned figure beside the shield. Burn fc1: 55 all-silhouette frames, WRONG 1 (1.8%), dead 9 (16%), vs visible-face frames WRONG 12/199 (6.0%), dead 58/199 (29%). The '9 of 68 dead' figure is 13% of dead frames from 21% of all frames. Mute corpus: 17 all-silhouette frames, dead 5 (29%), vs 40/621 (6.4%) with a visible face.
findings.impact: 81 beats in 2 configs: burn 53, flowers-in-the-attic 28 (published, so frozen). Silhouettes hide the face and expression, but none of the 53 burn beats had an authored expression, so invariant 1 is not broken. Whether silhouettes cost dead frames is unknown: burn says no, the corpus (n=17, 2 books) says yes. Smallest fix: when no cast is authored, the planner writes silhouette:false explicitly for illustration/diorama, or the presets drop the default and only the `silhouette` shot keeps it. test-requirement-staging.js:164-189 checks slot geometry, not this default.

findings.claim: The neutral mouth (v1) is a faint U smile, and the flat fix v2 exists but is switched off. A test enforces that it stays off.
findings.evidence: src/engines/antidote/characters/Everyman.tsx:56-61: v1 'M176,214 Q200,220 224,214' (midpoint 3 units below the corners), v2 flat, NEUTRAL_MOUTH_VERSION = "v1". scripts/test-neutral-mouth.js:34 asserts the default stays v1, so the test must change with the switch. analyses.summary: I compared the three books' final storyboards (art.json + config.antidote.json) against every mute run and against framecheck fc1 (262 Burn beats). Authors write dead beats because the rules send every hard beat to the same fallback ("concept: null, stage the PEOPLE ... with a strong callout", storyboard.js:262-263). The rig cannot make that fallback carry an abstract claim. Measured, iconless frames are much more often dead than icon frames: Burn fc1 34% dead / 38% ADDS without an icon vs 22% / 74% with one; Art of Saying No (ASN) run3 9/26 iconless frames dead vs 0/4 with an icon. ASN authored a concept on only 25.6% of beats, had 0 own icons, and put a held object on 39.5% (phone 29). Its round-2 re-author of 130 bare-everyman beats followed exactly this fallback, and dead rose from 4 to 9. Burn is generic for a different reason. The vocabulary has no subject for its world (no sword/crown/god/magic/bond; sword is drawn but filtered out). Burn's bible has no Diem, the protagonist named in 37 beats. 46% of beats were left with no cast, so Luther leads 64.5% of frames. 51.3% of beats use the shared generic set (fire 9.9%, chains 9.1%, war 8.7%). Yet those over-cap icons were Burn's best performers (fire ADDS 85%, chains 83%, puppeteer 93%), so the 5% cap and the "icon test" push authors toward null, not toward better icons. Learned Optimism (LO) did not mainly win on authoring style. Its bible spine has descriptive chapter titles, and plan-antidote.js:960-965 prints the act as the HUD topic on every frame. ASN and Burn print "SETUP/DEVELOPMENT/TURN". LO's non-adding frames were therefore judged TEXT_ONLY (12/30) instead of NONE (dead 0/60 across two runs). Its book type also helped: named researchers (11 cast, top lead only 35% of frames), real experiments drawn as own icons (shuttleBox 14 uses, 5/5 ADDS in mute), 8% diagrams, and shotOverride on 47.6% of beats. LO also uses icons sparingly (35.8%) and still barely meets ADDS (60%), so it is text-carried too. Its pass came from the dead bar, not from pictures.

findings.claim: The rules route every beat without a literal icon to 'concept: null + people + strong callout'. That fallback is the measured dead-frame class.
findings.evidence: storyboard.js:254-263 (icon test, then 'If nothing reads literally: concept: null and stage the PEOPLE doing the idea ... with a strong callout. A wrong icon is worse than none.'). Burn fc1 (262 frames, judge-result-1..9 joined to final art.json): icon frames n=183 dead 41 (22%) ADDS 74%; no-icon frames n=79 dead 27 (34%) ADDS 38%. ASN run3: no-icon 26 frames, 9 dead (35%), 2 WRONG; icon 4 frames, 0 dead, 4/4 ADDS. Pooled 240 mute frames: no-icon ADDS 39% vs icon 75%. ASN dead frames all have concept null and cast everyman/boss/friend with a face only. Examples: scene-12 'worried and calm women' for 'the cost is staggering'; scene-60 closed eyes for 'A FLAT NO AT 4:55'; scene-159 a smiling standing woman for 'a healthy adult takes refusal'.
findings.impact: In ASN run3, 9/9 dead and 2/2 WRONG are iconless person frames. In Burn fc1, 27/68 dead (40%) come from 30% of the beats. AGENT_LOG 2026-10-16: ASN round 2 re-authored 130 beats along this fallback and dead went from 4 to 9.

findings.claim: LO's dead 0/60 is largely explained by a pipeline confound: its story-bible spine act names are chapter titles, and the planner prints them as the HUD topic on every frame. ASN and Burn print generic act labels.
findings.evidence: plan-antidote.js:960-965: hudTopic = ACT_AT(frame) first. LO config hud.topic takes 5 values like 'THE THREE DIMENSIONS OF EXPLANATORY STYLE' (58-68 scenes each). ASN and Burn topics are SETUP/DEVELOPMENT/TURN/CONSEQUENCE/CLOSE (story-bible.json spine[].act = 'setup' ...). The blind 'text' field in LO run2 contains the chapter title on every item. LO runs: TEXT_ONLY 12/30 and 12/30, NONE 0 and 0. ASN run3 NONE 9; Burn run5 NONE 7.
findings.impact: This probably converts most would-be dead frames in LO into TEXT_ONLY. How large the effect is is unknown without an A/B. It is a bible/planner difference, not an authoring one, so 'LO passed in one round' is weak evidence for LO's authoring style.

findings.claim: The vocabulary hides drawn icons the narration needs: 21 of the 71 SCENE_ICONS are never offered to any book because they lack a motif-world origin or shared-pool entry.
findings.evidence: storyboard.js:104-107 (firewallOk = motif-world origins + shared-generic-motifs). Filtered out for all three books: alarmClock, coffee, work, laptopMockup, school, ladder, summit, wallet, magnifier, sword, dominoCascade, icebergDepth, funnelTrap, car, subway, zap and others. Burn narration names sword/blade/weapon in 9 beats, but sword is filtered out. Offered lists are nearly identical across a self-help book and a fantasy book: 41 shared icons (+1 own for Burn, +4 for LO).
findings.impact: Authors get the same generic pool regardless of world. ASN used 20 of 41 offered icons and Burn 26 of 42. This explains the 'generic' feel more than author choice does.

findings.claim: Subjects the narration names that no icon can show. Burn: crowns/thrones, gods, magic, the bond, army, poison. ASN: calendar, request, guilt, boundary, boss/work, the account/withdrawal metaphor. LO: dogs, noise, brain.
findings.evidence: Narration regex counts on art.json. BURN: crown/queen/king/throne/heir 70 beats, bond/mate/compulsion/spell 61, magic/power 58, kill/death 52, war/battle/army 44, god/descended 37; no crown/god/magic/bond icon exists, so authors used chains (24) for bonds and war/shield (35 beats show a shield). Most frequent words on Burn iconless beats: magic 8, mortals 8, descended 7, kindred 5, bond 4, stone 4. ASN iconless beats: guilt 8, boundary 7+5, request 5, weekend 5, excuse 5, withdrawal 6, account 5. ASN mustSee includes 'a crowded calendar being cleared', but there is no calendar icon and ASN has no signatureObjects, hence no motifs.json. LO iconless beats: noise 7, brain 7, dogs 5.
findings.impact: These are the subjects of most of the dead or generic beats in the two failing books. Own-icon coverage is tiny: 8 books have motifs.json, with 27 icons in total.

findings.claim: The 5% icon cap and the NEVER-for lists push authors away from the icons that performed best. They offer no positive mapping.
findings.evidence: Rule at storyboard.js:264; merge only warns (line 638). Burn exceeded the cap on fire 26 (9.9%), chains 24 (9.1%), war 23 (8.7%), heart 16 (6.1%) and puppeteer 14 (5.3%). In fc1 those icons scored ADDS 85/83/65/81/93% with 1 WRONG each. Under-cap substitutes scored worse: target dead 50%, trophy 40%, shield 33%, game 3/3 WRONG and dead. data/icon-readings.json: 26 icon rows, 18 with neverFor, 0 with a positive 'use for' field; 46 of 71 SCENE_ICONS have no reading row. The rules also say 'A wrong icon is worse than none' twice.
findings.impact: Authors conclude 'avoid icons': ASN concept 25.6%, LO 35.8%. Yet iconless frames carry about half the ADDS rate of icon frames. The cap is not what makes Burn generic; the missing world icons are.

findings.claim: Cast and shot left to the engine. Burn authors left cast unset on 46% of beats, and its bible omits the protagonist, so one identity floods the film.
findings.evidence: Burn art.json: 121/263 beats have no cast field; expression missing on 69 and action on 71. Story-bible cast = luther, teller, taran, narrator. Diem appears 3 times in the bible but is named in 37 beats; 20 of those have no cast. Config: lead identity luther in 169/262 frames (64.5%). All 5 twoShots are engine-made with the same identity twice (scenes 146, 164, 165, 172, 173); fc1 6/6 twin frames dead, 2 WRONG. ASN: 0 beats left to the engine but everyman leads 76% of beats. 73 two-cast beats became 60 engine twoShots (26.9%), none authored, none twins. LO: 8 beats unset, 149 shotOverride (47.6%), set on 100%, top lead 35%.
findings.impact: The 6 twin frames are 9% of Burn's fc1 dead. The flooding by one lead is unquantified as a misread cause, but authored vs engine cast in fc1 differ only modestly (dead 25% vs 28%).

findings.claim: Authoring channels that never produce ADDS: diagrams, strike callouts and small held objects. Relationship staging is unusable as configured.
findings.evidence: Diagram frames sampled (ASN scene-212, Burn scene-16, LO scene-04) were all TEXT_ONLY. Strike: pooled 14 mute frames ADDS 14%, WRONG 3/14; fc1 13 frames ADDS 15%; ASN scene-36 'AN APPROVAL ADDICT' struck read as 'he is not an approval addict' (WRONG). ASN holds on 39.5% of beats; run3 frames with holds were dead 36% vs 26% without. Relationship staging was used 0 times in all three. All three story bibles have 0 'groups', which rules.md lines 305-306 require, plus a Gate B run.
findings.impact: Diagrams and strikes avoid dead frames but cap ADDS. They keep LO at exactly 60% ADDS (18/30 in both runs). Relationship staging, the only rule aimed at 'two people in a relation', cannot fire without bible work.

findings.claim: The rules sheet is the same for every book except the vocabulary and one cast paragraph. Every book, fiction or not, gets the same We Were Liars (fiction) reference.
findings.evidence: diff of the three rules.md files: only title, icons, sets, cast, own-icon section and FICTION paragraph differ (storyboard.js:278-280). Same policy 'baseline', codeSha 25224bad for Burn and LO (storyboard/policy.json); model 'unrecorded'.
findings.impact: Differences between books come from the bible (cast, spine, signatureObjects) and the vocabulary, not from the instructions. This supports fixing bible and vocabulary inputs rather than re-authoring rounds.

findings.claim: Callout concreteness does not separate LO from the failing books.
findings.evidence: Callouts with a number: ASN 5.6%, Burn 1.6%, LO 6.6%. With an abstract word: 8.8% / 8.2% / 8.3%. Mean words: 4.17 / 3.88 / 3.14. LO used strike 28 times (9.7%) vs 10 and 13.
findings.impact: Rules out callout wording as the main driver of LO's result.

openQuestions: Does HUD chapter-title text alone flip NONE to TEXT_ONLY? A paired A/B (same frames, generic vs descriptive spine act names) would size the confound before LO's pass is credited to authoring.

The ASN book folder is gone from books/. I analysed it from the render bundle commit a8ead688 (refs render/the-art-of-saying-no-seg1..10) and from a scratchpad snapshot of audit/mute. Did the uploaded film match that bundle exactly? Earlier ASN runs (run1, run2) were judged on art.json from before round 2, so the pooled per-feature rates use final features for those frames.

Should the 21 drawn-but-unoffered SCENE_ICONS (alarmClock, work, coffee, laptopMockup, ladder, sword, wallet ...) get motif-world origins so the firewall filter stops hiding them? That needs a firewall-policy decision.
Do judges for the different books run on the same model and prompt? LO run2 has only 1 NEUTRAL in 30 vs 9-11 in ASN and Burn. Judge variance across books is unknown.
Are Burn's 121 unset-cast beats an author omission or a response to Diem missing from the cast? The authored-K.json files do not record the reason.

analyses.summary:
Per-frame data: audit/mute/ and audit/framecheck/ no longer exist under C:/Users/savas/Cursor/Remotion/test/audit or any worktree. The audit dir's mtime is 19:24 today. I worked from the session snapshot instead (scratchpad/snap/audit, 86 judged mute runs, 34 books) using three throwaway scripts: scratchpad/meas-inv.js, meas-pairs.js and meas-binom.js.

1) Most of the noise comes from the describer, not the judge. When a second judge scores the same text description (F451 --vs runs, 60 pairs), the verdicts agree 92% (WRONG kappa 0.76, dead kappa 0.95). When the same frame is described again, verdicts agree only 40-63% (WRONG kappa 0.03-0.27, dead kappa 0.27-0.56).

2) The burn numbers hold up. fc1 and run5 match on 19/30 correctness verdicts and on 1 of run5's 6 WRONG frames; WRONG kappa is 0.10 and dead kappa 0.44.

3) Over 30 frames, sampling alone makes the WRONG bar a coin toss. A film whose per-frame WRONG chance is 2% / 3% / 5% passes WRONG<=1 with probability 0.88 / 0.77 / 0.55. The dead bar is harder still: at a 17% dead rate (the corpus mean after readcheck) it passes with probability 0.60, and at 26% (burn fc1) with 0.17. So the two failing books need no other explanation. The-art-of-saying-no WRONG 2/4/2 (variance 1.3 vs a binomial 2.4) and burn WRONG 4/3/6 (2.3 vs 3.7) and dead 7/9/7 (1.3 vs 5.7) are all within sampling + rater noise. Only the-art-of-saying-no's dead count 3/4/9 is borderline beyond noise (ratio 2.35, p about 0.1). Across the whole corpus, run-to-run swings are 3.0x (WRONG) and 4.8x (dead) larger than binomial, driven by a few books with big jumps (into-the-wild 27 WRONG in run2, god-sees dead 21, red-rising 14 to 0).

4) The two instruments may not be calibrated alike. On burn the mute runs count 13 WRONG in 90 frames, against 13 in 262 for the fc1 full pass. If 5% were the true rate, the chance of 13/90 is 0.0005. On the same frame numbers mute-only WRONG beats fc1-only WRONG 11 to 3 (McNemar p about 0.06). It is unknown whether that is the film changing between runs or chunked framecheck rating lower.

5) A report-only instrument good to +-2 points (95%) has to look at every beat, not a sample: a sample would need 457 frames at 5% WRONG and 1,848 at 26% dead, more beats than a film has. It also needs about 4 independent describer passes, one judge per pass. That is about 72 agent runs for a 262-beat film, against 2 runs for today's mute test or 18 for one fc1 pass.

6) Readcheck (text only) says almost nothing about mute verdicts. Readcheck flagged 58 of 720 matched frames. Those frames came out mute WRONG 12.1% of the time, against 7.1% for frames readcheck called CORRECT, and readcheck caught only 7 of 54 mute WRONG. On runs dated after the readcheck, it caught 2 of 16 (5.0% vs 3.2%).

findings.claim: Judge noise is small: two different judges scoring the SAME blind description agree on 92% of correctness verdicts and 93% of contribution verdicts.
findings.evidence: fahrenheit-451 run2 --vs run1 and run3 --vs run2. Each vs-label's own verdict was compared with the re-judgement of that same description inside the --vs run, 60 pairs (scratchpad/meas-pairs.js). WRONG: 8 both, 4 only the original judge, 0 only the vs-judge, kappa 0.76, positive agreement 80%. Dead: 11 both, 1 only original, kappa 0.95. Caveat: the vs-judge saw two descriptions side by side, so the setup differs, and the 4-to-0 asymmetry (binomial p about 0.125) hints the vs-judge marks WRONG less often.
findings.impact: The judge explains at most about 8% verdict disagreement, roughly 10-20% of total rater disagreement. Extra rater budget should go to describers, not judges.

findings.claim: Describer noise dominates: describing the same frame again flips the verdict on 37-60% of frames, and on WRONG the two passes barely agree beyond chance.
findings.evidence: mindfulness run1 vs run1-redesc (framesFrom=run1, 30 frames): correctness same 12/30, contribution same 18/30; WRONG 3 both / 11 only run1 / 3 only redesc (kappa 0.03); dead 10 both / 4 / 7 (kappa 0.27). burn fc1 vs run5 (same config, same frame numbers, identical describer/judge prompts per fc1/PROMPTS.md vs run5/PROMPTS.md): correctness 19/30, contribution 23/30; WRONG 1 both / 5 only run5 / 2 only fc1 (positive agreement 22%, kappa 0.10); dead 4 / 3 / 3 (positive agreement 57%, kappa 0.44).
findings.impact: Under a single pass, one frame's WRONG flag is closer to a lottery ticket than a finding. Of 8 frames either pass called WRONG on burn, only 1 was called WRONG by both. This confirms the AGENT_LOG figures '19/30, 1/6'.

findings.claim: The 30-frame WRONG<=1 bar cannot separate a 2% film from a 5% film: sampling alone passes them with probability 0.88 and 0.55.
findings.evidence: Binomial n=30 (scratchpad/meas-binom.js). P(W<=1): 1% 0.964, 2% 0.879, 3% 0.773, 5% 0.554, 7% 0.369, 10% 0.184. 90% range of W: 2% 0..2, 3% 0..3, 5% 0..4. Dead<=5: 10% 0.927, 15% 0.711, 17% 0.597, 20% 0.428, 26% 0.170. Joint pass (assuming independence): 3% WRONG / 17% dead 0.46, 5% / 26% 0.09. The finite-population correction for 262 beats is only x0.94.
findings.impact: A film at the target quality (about 3% WRONG, 10% dead) still fails about 28% of fresh runs (pass 0.716). A fail followed by a pass after a fix is weak evidence that the fix worked.

findings.claim: The run-to-run swings cited for the two books are fully explained by sampling plus rater noise. Only the-art-of-saying-no's dead count rises beyond it, and only borderline.
findings.evidence: Observed vs binomial variance at each book's mean rate (meas-binom.js). the-art-of-saying-no WRONG 2/4/2: 1.3 vs 2.4. Dead 3/4/9: 10.3 vs 4.4 (chi2 about 4.7, df 2, p about 0.1). burn WRONG 4/3/6: 2.3 vs 3.7; dead 7/9/7: 1.3 vs 5.7. learned-optimism WRONG 2/1, dead 0/0. Corpus (22 books with 2 or more fresh runs): WRONG dispersion ratio 2.98 (chi2 139.9, df 47), about 1.7 without into-the-wild (run2 = 27 WRONG); dead ratio 4.82 (chi2 202.5, df 42), driven by god-sees 3/21, red-rising 14/0, flowers 13/0/2, mindfulness 14/2/0.
findings.impact: For burn and the-art-of-saying-no, 100% of the WRONG variation fits noise. The 'mass re-authoring raised dead 4 to 9' effect is suggestive (about a 10% chance by noise) but not proven. learned-optimism's pass after one round is consistent with a film at about 5% WRONG getting a lucky draw (P about 0.55) and a genuinely low dead rate.

findings.claim: The mute runs and the fc1 framecheck may be calibrated differently on WRONG: on burn, mute runs give about 14% WRONG and the fc1 full pass gives 5%.
findings.evidence: burn mute run1/run3/run5 = 13 WRONG in 90 frames; fc1 = 13 in 262. If p = 5%, P(X>=13 in 90) = 0.0005. On the same frame numbers, mute-only WRONG 11 vs fc1-only 3 (McNemar about p=0.06). On run5 alone 6 vs 3 (5 vs 2 discordant). Dead counts match (23 vs 23 over the 90). run1 and run3 had other configs, so part of the gap may be the film changing.
findings.impact: If the gap is real, fc1's 5% understates the rate the mute test would measure, or vice versa. Absolute rates from the two tools should not be compared until an anchor run exists.

findings.claim: A report-only instrument reaching +-2 points (95%) has to look at every beat with about 4 independent describer passes; no 30-frame design gets there.
findings.evidence: Sampling alone, at k=1, needs n = 1.96^2·p(1-p)/0.02^2: 280 frames at 3%, 457 at 5%, 865 at 10%, 1,848 at 26%. That is more than the 213-359 beats a film has. With every beat checked, only rater noise remains: sd = sqrt(E[q(1-q)]/(N·k)). E[q(1-q)] = (disagreement rate)/2, estimated from fc1-vs-run5 (WRONG 7/30 gives 0.117, dead 6/30 gives 0.10). For N=262: WRONG sd 2.1 pt at k=1, 1.2 at k=3, 1.06 at k=4 (+-2.1), 0.94 at k=5. Dead sd 1.95 at k=1, 0.98 at k=4 (+-1.9).
findings.impact: Proposed rule (report-only, bars untouched): every beat checked, k=4 fresh describers per frame, 1 judge per description, rate = mean of passes with a CI, and a per-frame finding only when 2 or more of 4 (or 2 of 3) passes agree. Cost: 9 describers + 9 judges = 18 agent runs per pass (chunk 30), about 72 runs for a 262-beat film plus one still render (~1 h per runbook §3b; extra passes reuse the stills). Today's mute test is 2 runs and one fc1 pass is 18. Token cost per agent run is unknown.

findings.claim: Readcheck verdicts barely predict mute verdicts: about 87% of mute WRONG frames sit on beats readcheck read as CORRECT.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/meas-readcheck.js over the 12 books with a full readcheck (n>=150) and matching mute runs, 720 frames. Readcheck WRONG frames: mute WRONG 4/24 (16.7%). NEUTRAL: 3/34 (8.8%). CORRECT: 47/662 (7.1%). Readcheck caught 7/54 mute WRONG. On runs dated after the readcheck file (480 frames): 2/40 (5.0%) vs 14/440 (3.2%), catching 2/16. Dead: 14/58 (24%) vs 112/662 (16.9%). the-art-of-saying-no readcheck has 0 WRONG / 16 NEUTRAL in 223 beats, while its mute runs had 2/4/2 WRONG.
findings.impact: A clean readcheck says nearly nothing about the mute result. The mute misreads are visual (face, staging, icon), not textual, which is consistent with the beard/twoShot/closed-eye findings.

findings.evidence: snap/books/*/readcheck.json: burn n=1, i-robot 1, long-way-down 1, stolen-focus 1 (the full run survives only as readcheck.full-run2.json), red-rising 1, wonder 2, mindfulness 2, die-with-zero 2, and others. The current scripts/readcheck.js tally merges rechecks, so these are probably from older code or partial preps (unknown).

analyses.summary:
I counted 30 Antidote books from 2026-09-24 on. I merged data/engine-outcomes.json (which stops on 10-03), books/*/mute-test.json and the AGENT_LOG entries in both checkouts. Together they hold 81 fresh-holdout mute runs, 2.70 per book. Only 9 of 30 books passed on run 1. Another 7 passed later, after 2–6 runs. The other 14 were shipped with the mute test failing (operator override) or parked (burn). Those 14 used 46 of the 81 runs, so 57% of all mute spend went to books that never passed.

Fix rounds do not measurably help. Of 51 consecutive run pairs, 24 improved, 23 got worse on WRONG or dead, and 7 stayed flat. That is a coin flip, and it fits the measured rater noise: 19/30 verdicts agreed on burn fc1, and P0.1 agreement was 0.82–0.87. Under a binomial model, a book whose true WRONG rate is 5% passes WRONG ≤1 on 30 frames only 55% of the time. At the 26% dead rate measured on burn, dead ≤5 passes 17% of the time. So a 'PASS@N' after several rounds is largely resampling.

The text-only readcheck does not predict the mute verdict either. Books that passed had 0–5.6% readcheck WRONG. Books that failed had 0–1.1%. The failures the mute test does find point at the engine, not the storyboard: beard drawn as a grin, duplicate-identity twoShot, narrator injected on cast=[] beats, the stagnation engine rewriting faces, no ghost mode, text drawn over faces. Most of these are still open in the current code.

Recent books (2026-10-03 on) did worse than the corpus: 16 books, 39 runs, 7 passes. Firewall REVIEW triage (373–678 per book) blocked at least 7 books for agent time. 6 of those 7 were published anyway, and on 10-16 the operator changed the policy to 'noBlock'.

analyses.summary:
Data source: the main checkout has no audit/mute/ folder and is missing several book folders, such as books/the-art-of-saying-no. I used the full snapshot at scratchpad/snap/ (books/, audit/mute/, audit/framecheck/). That gave 30 Antidote books with a config and mute history, and 2,070 judged mute frames (79 runs) joined to config scenes.

Outcomes: 8 books passed on their first fresh holdout (P1), 9 passed after fixes (Pfix), and 13 never passed (F). By book type, fiction passed first time 3/17 (18%) against nonfiction 5/13 (38%), and passed at some point 9/17 against 8/13. Per frame, fiction is only slightly worse: WRONG 10.3% vs 8.0%, dead 14.4% vs 11.7%. So book type explains part of the outcome, not most of it.

Book-level staging features separate passing from failing books only weakly. The largest effect sizes between P1 and F: share of idle cast d=-1.39, physical-action share d=+1.09, all-neutral faces d=+1.14 (the wrong direction for the beard theory). Every other feature has |d| < 1, and each group has only 8-13 books.

Luck is large. To pass W ≤ 1/30 a book needs a true WRONG rate of about 3% or less: P(pass) is 74% at 3.3%, 55% at 5% and 20% at the pooled 9.6%. All 8 P1 books were sampled exactly once. Repeat samples of what was most likely the same film swing widely: 21-days run2 W7 then run1 W1 PASS seven minutes later; Southern Book Club W 0/5/10/6 within 1 hour; Fahrenheit holdouts W 7/5/8/1. The spread is about twice the binomial standard deviation.

Learned-optimism's pass is essentially a coin flip. Its pooled WRONG rate is 5.0%, so P(pass) ≈ 0.55, and run2 came 35 minutes after run1 with only 2 of 313 beats changed.

At frame level, what does separate good from bad is clear:
- **Own icons in fiction:** WRONG 0% / dead 2.9% / ADDS 91% (n=34) vs 5.2% / 7.5% / 63.5%.
- **Diagrams:** WRONG 1.4%, dead 0% (n=70).
- **twoShot in fiction:** WRONG 13.5% vs 3.5% (n=52), about 3.9x.
- **Beard:** frames with a stubble or full beard read as smiling 21.8% of the time vs 6.6% without (n=354 vs 1,341). An unintended smile raises WRONG to 21.2% vs 9.0%.
- **Fiction WRONG:** driven by faces (38 of 136 'sees' lines mention a smile).
- **Nonfiction WRONG:** driven by text (42 of 60).

Burn-of-the-everflame fails on dead frames more than on WRONG. Framecheck over the whole film gives WRONG 5.0% and dead 26%, so P(pass one run) ≈ 0.55 × 0.17 = 0.09. It also has the lowest interaction staging of any fiction book: 3.4% of beats have more than one character, and 10.6% of cast use physical actions. relationshipStaging is used in 0 of 46 Antidote configs.

findings.claim: Passing the 30-frame holdout is to a large degree a sampling and rater lottery, not proof of a better film. Repeat samples of what was most likely the same render differ far more than a binomial would.
findings.evidence:
snap/books/*/mute-test.json run dates:
- 21-days-of-fear: run2 13:52 W7 dead4 FAIL, then run1 13:59 W1 PASS. No fix round fits in 7 minutes, and the passing run was labelled run1 after run2.
- Southern Book Club runs 4-7 (10:52-11:50): W 0, 5, 10, 6. Observed sd ≈ 4.1 vs binomial sd ≈ 2.1 at p=0.175.
- Fahrenheit: holdout1 and holdout2 in the same minute (W 7, 5), holdout3 W8, holdout4 W1 PASS 37 minutes later.
- Unhinged: run5 W3, then run6 W1 ten minutes later.
Binomial P(W ≤ 1 of 30): 0.736 at p=1/30, 0.554 at p=0.05, 0.202 at the pooled Antidote p=0.096. Burn: framecheck fc1 vs mute run5 agree on 19/30 correctness verdicts (re-verified with scratchpad/cfm-snap.js; run1 and run3 agree 18/30).
findings.impact: All 8 first-pass books (great-at-work, i-robot, piranesi, skin-in-the-game, stolen-focus, courage, paradox, we-were-liars) were sampled only once (mean 1.0 fresh runs vs 3.4 for the other groups). At least 3 never-pass books had a pooled-rate P(pass) of 0.35-0.40 (die-with-zero, wonder, long-way-down). A one-run PASS does not separate a book at 2% WRONG from one at 5%.

findings.claim: Learned-optimism's PASS is not evidence that its fix round worked. It is a second draw from a film whose true WRONG rate is about 5%.
findings.evidence: snap/audit/mute/learned-optimism.../run1: W2 dead0 at 11:01. run2: W1 dead0 PASS at 11:36. AGENT_LOG.md says only beats 189 and 277 of 313 changed between them. Pooled over 60 frames: WRONG 3/60 = 5.0%, so P(pass one run) ≈ 0.55. Static staging is ordinary: concept share 0.36, own-icon share 0.07, person-only share 0.56.
findings.impact: Do not copy learned-optimism's authoring as a recipe. Changing 2 of 313 beats moves a fresh-sample rate by about 0.6% at most.

findings.claim: Book type (argument non-fiction vs narrative fiction) explains a modest part of passing. Per frame, the two types are much closer than the pass rates suggest.
findings.evidence:
Book level (30 Antidote books):
- Fiction: 17 books, P1 3, Pfix 6, F 8 (first-pass 18%, ever-pass 53%).
- Nonfiction: 13 books, P1 5, Pfix 3, F 5 (first-pass 38%, ever-pass 62%).
Frame level (n=1,320 fiction, 750 nonfiction): WRONG 10.3% vs 8.0% (1.3x), dead 14.4% vs 11.7%.
The largest structural differences between types:
- idle cast share: 0.185 fiction vs 0.074 nonfiction, d=-1.12
- concept share: 0.444 vs 0.301, d=-1.02 (fiction uses more generic icons)
- person-only share: 0.52 vs 0.66, d=+0.99
findings.impact: Book type explains roughly the 20-point gap in first-pass rate. It does not explain within-type failures: 5 of 13 nonfiction books never passed (die-with-zero, don't-believe, art-of-saying-no, mindfulness, second-mountain).

findings.claim: Static book-level staging features separate passing from failing books only weakly. The strongest is how much the cast DOES, not icon share.
findings.evidence:
Cohen's d, P1 (n=8) vs F (n=13), from scratchpad/sc-contrast2.js:
- idle share: 0.063 vs 0.201, d=-1.39
- physical-action share (walk/sit/hold/reach/fight etc.): 0.275 vs 0.197, d=+1.09
- all-neutral faces: 0.388 vs 0.243, d=+1.14
- distinct cast: 11.1 vs 7.1, d=+0.91
- all others |d| < 0.6: concept 0.394 vs 0.343 (d=0.33), own icons 0.059 vs 0.074 (d=-0.21), twoShot 0.082 vs 0.111 (d=-0.34), silhouette 0.031 vs 0.035, diagram 0.037 vs 0.031, mean beat 9.10 s vs 8.88 s.
Within fiction (ever-pass vs F): concept 0.508 vs 0.372 (d=0.85), person-only 0.457 vs 0.591 (d=-0.84).
Within nonfiction (ever-pass vs F): diorama 0.174 vs 0.392 (d=-0.78).
findings.impact: No single storyboard share predicts PASS. Fiction passers carry more beats with a visual subject; nonfiction failures overuse diorama. Feature values come from the final config, not the config at each run.

findings.claim: At frame level, own (book-specific) icons and diagrams are the strongest positive levers. twoShot, silhouette and all-neutral faces are the strongest negative ones, especially in fiction.
findings.evidence:
Last-run frames, where the config matches the run (n=750):
- Fiction own-icon: WRONG 0%, dead 2.9%, ADDS 91.2% (n=34) vs 5.2%, 7.5%, 63.5%.
- Fiction concept present: ADDS 85% vs 52%.
- Fiction twoShot: WRONG 13.5%, dead 15.4% (n=52) vs 3.5%, 6.0%.
- Fiction silhouette: ADDS 26.7%, WRONG 13.3% (n=15).
- All-neutral faces: WRONG 8.9% fiction and 8.2% nonfiction vs 3.2% and 3.4%.
All runs (n=2,100):
- Diagram: WRONG 1.4%, dead 0% (n=70).
- Nonfiction diorama: dead 25.2% (n=230) vs illustration 7.0% (n=115).
- Nonfiction closeUp: dead 28.9% (n=45).
findings.impact: For burn: only 2% of beats use an own icon (1 motif) vs 7-23% in other fiction books; twoShot is 2% (6 of them same-identity twins); 41% of faces are all-neutral. Each of these is a measured WRONG or dead driver.

findings.claim: The beard-as-grin defect holds across the whole corpus, not just burn, and fiction pays for it more.
findings.evidence:
scratchpad/sc5.js: frames with cast and no happy/smirk configured, beard taken from story-bible cast variant.beard:
- With a beard: seen 'smiling' 21.8% (n=354; stubble 23.2% of 293, full 19.4% of 31).
- Without a beard: 6.6% (n=1,341).
- Neutral-only faces: 24.3% vs 10.7%.
- An unintended smile raises WRONG to 21.2% vs 9.0% (n=165 vs 1,530).
- Unintended-smile rate: fiction 11.9% vs nonfiction 5.8%. Highest books: unhinged 22.8%, the-hate-u-give 18.5%, 21-days 14.6%, fahrenheit 13.7%.
- A smile appears in the 'sees' line of 38 of 136 fiction WRONG vs 6 of 60 nonfiction WRONG.
- 42 of 60 nonfiction WRONG judge notes cite text (strike-through or negation 16 of 60).
findings.impact: Fixing face rendering (beard over mouth, a neutral that cannot read as a smile) targets the largest single fiction WRONG class: about 28% of fiction WRONG frames.

findings.claim: What a fiction book like burn needs that the engine cannot draw today. Ranked by the measured cause classes above, these are engine capabilities, not storyboard rewrites.
findings.evidence:

plans.thesis: The largest code-side lever is to stop the engine from contradicting the narration on its own: the face (beard and neutral mouth read as a grin), the twin-cast fill and its false authorship lock, and the strike that viewers read as the claim. Together these are about 30 of the 46 WRONG items in the cause map. Smile alone shows up in 38 of 136 fiction WRONG "sees" lines, and strike or rejected-premise accounts for 14 of 29 non-burn WRONG. The second lever is drawing capability. Iconless frames are dead 9.4% vs 5.1% and ADD only 39% vs 75%, and fiction own-icon frames are WRONG 0% / ADDS 91%. Yet 21 drawn icons are hidden by the firewall filter, and fantasy worlds have no crown, god, magic or bond icon. A 10x drop is plausible only inside specific classes: twins go from 20 locked beats to 0, game-reads-as-trophy goes from 3 of 3 WRONG to 0, and beard grin can fall to the beardless baseline, about 3x. For whole-film WRONG and dead, the honest expectation is about 1.5-2.5x, because 64% of dead is still authoring (bare figure with no object). The 10x is in wasted effort: one engine fix replaces the fix rounds that today move WRONG or dead the wrong way 23 of 51 times. Each fix is checked on a blind component sheet, not by re-running the noisy 30-frame verdict. That sheet uses the bars it would use anyway. Before any of this, the measurement corpus has to be secured: it now exists only in stash@{0}.

plans.thesis: The biggest gain is to stop asking authors to fix things they cannot fix. Then give them a picture for what the narration names, and let them change only what someone has actually seen in a real frame. Authoring problems account for 28% of WRONG and 64% of dead. Most of the dead come from one source: the rule at scripts/storyboard.js:262-263 ("concept: null and stage the PEOPLE ... with a strong callout"). It produces bare-figure frames, 35 of the 48 dead frames outside burn. Iconless frames read much worse: ADDS 39% against 75%, and burn fc1 dead 34% against 22%. So the vocabulary has to cover each book's world (own icons drawn from the beats that have no icon, the 21 icons that are drawn but hidden, broken or negated icon states), and the rules have to require a visual carrier instead of steering authors toward "no icon". Engine defects cause 46% of WRONG (beard grin, twin cast, v1 mouth, trophy drawn for `game`). They must be fixed once in code before any authoring round, because no amount of re-authoring touches them: burn's 187 patched beats moved nothing. Last, the fix round becomes closed-loop. Run framecheck, act only on findings that two blind passes agree on or that the author confirmed by looking at the still, sort each finding by owner, and fix its cause class through similar-candidates. That replaces blind mass re-authoring: the 130-beat ASN round raised dead from 4 to 9, and 23 of 51 rounds made things worse. A 10x drop in effort per book is plausible. A 10x drop in misreads is not: about 13% of WRONG are rater errors, and a 30-frame run cannot tell 2% from 5%. Realistic targets are about 2-2.5x fewer WRONG and 2-3x fewer dead.

items.title: 2. Replace the 'concept: null + people + strong callout' fallback with a required visual carrier
items.what: Rewrite the icon-test block in scripts/storyboard.js:254-264. Every beat must name a CARRIER: an own icon, a shared icon whose positive reading fits, a held signature object, a diagram, or a physical action from the measured-readable set. 'A wrong icon is worse than none' stays, but the fallback becomes 'draw it (item 3) or pick a diagram', not 'bare figure'. Turn the 5%-per-icon cap into a soft warning tied to icon-readings precision, because over-cap fire, chains and puppeteer scored ADDS 83-93%. Add a positive `useFor` field to data/icon-readings.json; 26 rows exist, 18 have neverFor, 0 have useFor. Merge lint (storyboard.js merge): a beat with concept null, no holds of a signature object, no diagram and an idle or talk action is reported as CARRIERLESS with a count. It is a warning, not a block.
items.evidence: In the 23 non-burn books, bare-figure-no-object is 35/48 dead and dead is 85% authoring-owned. Latest-run frames: no-icon frames dead 9.4% / WRONG 5.9% (n=425) vs icon frames 5.1% / 3.4%. Burn fc1: 34% / ADDS 38% vs 22% / 74%. ASN run3: 9/9 dead were iconless person frames. ASN authored a concept on only 25.6% of beats. Diagrams: WRONG 1.4%, dead 0% (n=70).
items.expectedEffect: If carrierless beats fall from about 59% of frames to about 25% at today's per-frame rates, the corpus dead rate falls from 7.6% toward about 5.5%, and ADDS moves toward the icon-frame rate (+15-20 points). Larger gains need item 3, because the carrier has to exist. Dead on non-fiction about 1.5-2x lower; not 10x.
items.howWeMeasure: CARRIERLESS share per new book at merge, a structural count that needs no rater. Dead and ADDS on fresh mute holdouts of the next new books against the corpus base rates (dead 7.6%, ADDS by type). The CARRIERLESS lint is reported, not tuned against the mute sample.
items.risk: Authors may force weak icons to satisfy the lint, which pushes generic-icon dead and icon-polarity WRONG up (28 dead, 4 WRONG today). Mitigation: the lint accepts a diagram or an action, and icon-readings neverFor stays in force.
items.respectsRules: Changes instructions and a report-only lint, not bars. Authored choices remain final. Applies to new books only.

items.title: 3. Make each book's world drawable: own icons from the gap list, unhide the 21 hidden icons, add broken and negated states
items.what: (a) `storyboard.js prep` computes a GAP LIST: the most frequent narration nouns on beats whose draft has no fitting icon, e.g. burn crown/throne 70, bond 61, magic 58, god 37; ASN guilt 8, boundary 12, calendar (in mustSee). prep then refuses to continue until the top gaps (e.g. ≥8 beats each) are drawn as own icons in motifs.json, or are waived with a reason via the existing --skip-own-icons. It extends the signatureObjects stop at storyboard.js:435-437, which today only warns when signatureObjects is empty (ASN had 0). (b) Ask the operator, who owns the firewall-policy decision, to register motif-world origins for the 21 SCENE_ICONS filtered out at storyboard.js:104-107 (sword, wallet, alarmClock, calendar-like, ladder, work ...), so books whose world fits can use them. (c) Allow polarity variants in the motifs.json schema (`broken`, `struck`, `empty`, e.g. a snapped chain, cracked trophy, burned house) as data paths through customSvg. Name each variant blind on own-icons-sheet.js.
items.evidence: Own icons in fiction: WRONG 0%, dead 2.9%, ADDS 91% (n=34) vs 5.2% / 7.5% / 63.5%. Learned Optimism's shuttleBox: 5/5 ADDS. Only 8 books have motifs.json (27 icons); burn has 1 motif vs 3-6 in fiction books that passed. The offered vocabulary is nearly the same for a self-help book and a fantasy book (41 shared icons). Sword is drawn but filtered, while burn names blades in 9 beats. Generic-icon dead 28 (8 vocabulary gaps). Icon polarity: 4 WRONG + 3 dead, and no broken variant exists anywhere.
items.expectedEffect: This is the main dead-frame lever for fiction and speculative worlds. If own and world-fit icons go from about 2-7% to about 25% of beats at the measured own-icon rates, fiction dead could fall by about half and icon-polarity WRONG to about 0. Burn-like books: dead 26% → an estimated 12-15%; it cannot reach the ≤10% zone without item 1's twin fix and authored cast. items.howWeMeasure: Structural: own-icon share and the uncovered-gap count per new book at merge. Quality: blind own-icons-sheet names must match the meaning before use (existing loop). Then ADDS and dead on fresh mute holdouts of new books, broken down by own vs shared icon frames, against the per-frame baselines above.
items.risk: Badly drawn icons misread (SBC casserole read as 'toaster', a dopamineHook read as 'noose'). The blind sheet is the guard. The firewall-origin change is an operator policy decision. Polarity variants need a blind check, because 'broken' may read as 'old'.
items.respectsRules: Data plus prep stops; no engine restaging; no bar change. Authored concepts render unchanged through customSvg. New books only.

items.title: 4. Negation grammar: forbid rejected-premise callouts and partial strikes; add a deterministic stance lint
items.what: Rules sheet: a callout must state the claim the narration affirms. When the narration rejects X, show 'NOT X → Y' with both parts, or Y alone, never X alone. A strike must cover a whole verbatim phrase and always sit next to the affirmed replacement. Merge lint in storyboard.js: flag a callout whose tokens appear in the narration window inside a negation scope (not / never / isn't / rather than / myth / wrong to). Also flag a strike with no unstruck companion and a partial strike inside a sentence. Engine follow-up, for review only: strike visibility, since in 2 cases the strike was not seen at all. Keep the existing verbatim rule (visual-strategy.js:68/282) but report demotions instead of silently dropping them.
items.evidence: Strike-negation is the largest non-burn WRONG class: 9 of 29. Strike frames: WRONG 9.9% vs 4.2% (n=81), ADDS 14-15%. Rejected-premise callouts: 5/29 non-burn WRONG. Together they make up 14/29 (48%) of non-burn WRONG. Readcheck had 0 WRONG on ASN before every failing run and catches 7/54 mute WRONG overall, so the existing text check does not see stance. Example: miracle shipped 81 inverted strikes.
items.expectedEffect: Non-fiction WRONG: if the lint removes about 70% of these 14 items, non-burn WRONG falls about 33% (29 → about 19 items). Non-fiction per-frame WRONG 8.0% → about 5%. This is the largest WRONG lever for argument books. Also less wasted effort: no strike re-authoring rounds like miracle's 65 beats.
items.howWeMeasure: Lint hit count at merge on new books (structural). Strike-frame and negation-callout WRONG rate on fresh mute holdouts against the 9.9% baseline. The judge prompt is not changed.
items.risk: False positives on incidental negations, the same failure as love-hypothesis #2 (~66 beats). Keep it a warning with a per-beat waive reason. Removing strikes may push frames toward TEXT_ONLY.
items.respectsRules: Does not touch the rater prompt (strike literacy stays an operator decision under rule 2). Authoring rules and a lint only. Authored text is unchanged by the engine.

items.title: 5. Story-bible completeness gate: every named lead in the cast, every beat cast-authored, descriptive spine acts
items.what: storyboard.js prep: refuse when a person named in at least N beats of the narration (e.g. ≥10) is not a bible cast key. Burn's Diem is named in 37 beats but is not in the bible. merge: report beats with no `cast` field (burn 121/263), and require an explicit `cast: []` for an intentionally empty stage, so no engine fill happens silently. Bible template: spine acts get descriptive chapter names instead of setup/turn labels, because plan-antidote.js:960-965 prints the act as the HUD topic on every frame. Optional: a `groups` field so relationship staging can fire later.
items.evidence: Burn: cast unauthored on 113-121 of 263 beats; that alone produced the twin, silhouette and engine-filled classes. Luther leads 64.5% of frames, and in fc1 twoShot frames were 100% dead. Recent fully authored books leave only 0-5 beats unauthored. LO's descriptive acts became the HUD on every frame, and LO had 0/60 dead (TEXT_ONLY 12/30), while ASN and burn print SETUP/TURN. Relationship staging was used 0 times in 46 configs, and 0 bibles have groups.
items.expectedEffect: Removes the burn-type outlier: the engine-filled classes are 16 of burn's dead plus 2 WRONG, about 25% of its dead. The HUD-topic effect on dead is unknown and needs an A/B before it is credited. It may convert some NONE frames to TEXT_ONLY, which lowers dead without raising ADDS, so it is reported honestly as text-carried.
items.howWeMeasure: Structural at prep and merge: unnamed-lead count and unauthored-cast count. For the HUD effect: an A/B on a not-yet-published book, the same beats rendered with generic vs descriptive act names, each judged by fresh describers. It is report-only and is not the verdict.
items.risk: The HUD chapter text could be seen as gaming the dead bar. It is legitimate on-screen information, but report it as TEXT_ONLY and not as image ADDS. A threshold set too low forces minor names into the cast.
items.respectsRules: The bar and its computation are unchanged; the judge reads whatever is on screen, as before. Authorship becomes more explicit, which fits invariant 1. New books only.

items.title: 6. Look before authoring: blind cast/expression and pose sheets, the same loop as own-icons-sheet
items.what: Extend own-icons-sheet.js, or add a sibling cast-sheet in the same headless-Chrome way with no bundle. It draws every bible cast member (with variant, beard and outfit) × the 9 faces, plus the action vocabulary (think, slump, point, hold ...), on numbered sheets. A fresh sonnet agent names mood and action blind. A cast member is approved only when the names match. Mismatches are recorded as icon-readings staging rows, which reach every rules.md (invariant 5), and as engine for-review items.
items.evidence: The beard grin was found only after several failed mute runs on several books (beloved scene-208, love-hypothesis, burn). 'think' reads as pointing 24% of the time (23/94), and as thinking 1/94. 'slump' reads only as standing 48% of the time, and as slumped 4.6%. own-icons-sheet already caught casserole→'toaster' and hook→'noose' in seconds.
items.expectedEffect: Catches face and pose defects at book setup in minutes, instead of after 3-6 mute runs. Recent books used 2.4 runs per book (39 runs / 16 books), and 57% of runs went to books that never passed. Per new book, about 1 agent run replaces the 1-3 rounds spent finding the same class. Wasted effort for this class falls by about 5-10x. The per-frame misread gain is counted in item 1.
items.howWeMeasure: Number of face and pose misreads first found by a mute or framecheck run versus first found on the sheet, tracked per new book in AGENT_LOG. Target: sheet first in most cases.
items.risk: A static sheet misses context effects such as framing and crops (fc1 scene-177 cropped collapse) and blink timing (scene-162). It complements framecheck but does not replace it.
items.respectsRules: Read-only rendering of the vocabulary; no bar change; no staging override.

items.title: 7. Closed-loop fix round: framecheck findings confirmed twice, sorted by owner, fixed by cause class with a beat cap
items.what: Codify in STORYBOARD_RUNBOOK §3b/§5 and preview-hazirla. After the first failed mute run (or before the first one, for fiction), run framecheck on all beats, with a 2nd describer pass optional for the flagged beats. Accept a per-frame finding only when 2 passes agree, or when the author opened the still and confirmed what it shows. Sort each finding as ENGINE (goes to for-review, never into the storyboard), VOCABULARY (goes to item 3) or AUTHORING. For AUTHORING findings, use similar-candidates.js to change only beats that share the confirmed staging, and report the number of changed beats (soft cap, e.g. ≤25, waivable with a reason). Forbid a new mute holdout until something has changed. 21-days was re-sampled 7 minutes later and flipped W7 → W1.
items.evidence: Of 51 run-to-run transitions, 24 improved and 23 got worse. Mass rounds failed: burn 187 beats, W 4→3→6; ASN 130 beats, dead 4→9. Small cause-class fixes did better: LO 2 beats, long-way-down 8 beats dead 7→0, red-rising 19 icons dead 14→0, although each is weak on its own. Describer noise: WRONG kappa 0.03-0.27. Judge noise is small (92% agreement). One framecheck is 18 agents, about the cost of the 9 mute runs a never-passing book burns.
items.expectedEffect: Beats re-authored per round: from 94-130 to about 10-25, roughly 5-10x less effort. Fewer harmful rounds (today 23/51 get worse), because unconfirmed single-pass findings, at 22% WRONG positive agreement, no longer drive edits. The fresh mute holdout stays the only verdict.
items.howWeMeasure: Per new book: beats changed per round, mute runs to PASS or operator decision, and the sign of the change between runs. Compare with the cost-process baseline: 2.70 runs per book, 57% of runs on never-passing books. The verdict is always a fresh holdout. Confirmed framecheck re-checks of changed beats are logged as diagnostics only.
items.risk: Framecheck costs about 1 h of render plus 18-36 agents, so it is too heavy for every book. Use it for fiction or after a first failure. The mute and fc1 calibration gap on burn (13/90 vs 13/262 WRONG) means its absolute rates must not be compared with mute rates.
items.respectsRules: The verdict remains a fresh mute holdout (rule 3). Re-checks of fixed beats are never the verdict. Engine failures are routed to for-review and not patched in the storyboard. No bar or sampling change.

notDoing: Changing the 30-frame sample size, repeating samples for the verdict, or adding strike literacy or a chrome preamble to the rater prompt. The binomial math shows the WRONG ≤1/30 bar cannot separate 2% from 5% (P pass 0.88 vs 0.55), but how the bar is computed is an operator decision (rule 2). Flag it; do not do it.
Another mass re-authoring round on any book. ASN's 130 beats moved dead 4→9, burn's 187 patched beats moved WRONG 4→3→6, and 23 of 51 rounds got worse.

Spending more agents on the text-only readcheck as a predictor. It caught 7/54 mute WRONG overall (2/16 on runs after the readcheck), and ASN had 0 readcheck WRONG before 3 failing runs. Keep it as a cheap text sanity check only.

Prioritising the silhouette default fix. The claim that silhouettes are 'mostly dead' is refuted on burn (16% dead vs 28.5%), the corpus sample is n=17 from 2 books, and 28 of the 81 affected beats are in frozen flowers-in-the-attic.
Triage by config risk flags. The best top-third catches only 47% of WRONG, which is barely better than random at the volume needed.

Copying Learned Optimism's authoring as a recipe. Its pass is about a coin flip at a pooled 5% WRONG, only 2 of 313 beats changed, and its 0 dead is partly the descriptive HUD topic, which is a pipeline effect.

Building generic relationship staging and two-body verbs now. It is used 0 times in 46 configs, the schema has 2 mechanisms, and it needs new engine rig work plus bible groups. Its value is unmeasured, so do it after items 1-5.
Retrofitting or re-planning published books (flowers, a-good-man, beloved and others), even though they carry the twin and silhouette defects. They are frozen, and their configs remain the record.
Spending agent sessions on firewall REVIEW triage. 6 of 7 blocked books shipped anyway, precision was 37% on Beloved, and the operator already set noBlock.
Treating framecheck rates as comparable to mute rates. On burn, 13/90 vs 13/262 WRONG (p≈0.0005 if 5%) is unexplained, so it needs an anchor run first.

plans.thesis: The one move with the biggest multiplier is to stop judging fixes with a single 30-frame draw and work from a cause ledger. At a 5% true WRONG rate, 30 frames pass about 55% of the time. Two describer passes agreed on 1 of 6 WRONG. 23 of 51 fix rounds made things worse. 57% of all mute runs (46 of 81) went to books that never passed. So most of today's effort is chasing noise. Instead, measure once per engine release over the whole film with repeat describers (report-only), and fix only the cause classes that show up in both passes. Those are mostly engine classes: the beard drawn as a grin, twin cast in two-person shots, the trophy icon, and how negation is shown. One code fix of each helps every new book, and only then does one fresh mute holdout serve as the verdict. A 10x cut in wasted effort (fix rounds, re-authoring, readcheck agents) is plausible. A 10x cut in misreads is not. Fixing the measured classes should cut WRONG by roughly 1.5-2.5x and dead by roughly 1.5-2x.
