items.title: 3. Release-level measurement protocol (report-only) that replaces repeated 30-frame fix rounds
items.what: Add a scripts/framecheck.js mode `--passes=2` (chunk 30, fresh describer per chunk per pass, one judge per description). It stores pass-level results plus per-class tallies with binomial CIs, and per-frame findings only where both passes agree. Run it once per engine release on one reference book (burn, parked), not per book. Add a runbook rule: no fresh mute holdout on a film that has not changed since the last one (the 21-days run1/run2 7-minute case). A failed mute holdout feeds the cause ledger in item 4, not an immediate re-author and re-sample. Keep mute-test.js, its 30 frames, its bars and its rater prompt exactly as they are.
items.evidence: Describer noise dominates. A re-description flips the verdict on 37-60% of frames (WRONG kappa 0.03-0.27). Re-judging the same description agrees 92% (kappa 0.76). On 30 frames, P(W≤1) is 0.88 at 2%, 0.55 at 5% and 0.18 at 10%. Run-to-run dispersion is 3.0x binomial for WRONG and 4.8x for dead. Of 51 run-to-run transitions, 24 improved and 23 got worse. Precision of ±2 points needs every beat × about 4 describer passes, and no 30-frame design gets there. Mute runs vs fc1 on burn: 13/90 vs 13/262 WRONG, an unresolved calibration gap.
items.expectedEffect: Mute runs per book: 2.70 now, about 1.2-1.5 expected. Rounds on books that never pass stop being repeated, cutting the 57% of runs that were wasted. Per-frame findings from 2-of-2 agreement drop false leads. In fc1 vs run5, 7 of 8 WRONG flags were single-pass only, so about 85% of WRONG leads were not reproducible. Agent cost: about 36 runs per release instead of about 9 mute runs plus fix rounds per failing book. This is where a 10x reduction in wasted effort is plausible.
items.howWeMeasure: Track mute runs and fix rounds per new book against the 30-book baseline (2.70 runs, 9/30 first-pass). Track the share of fix rounds whose next fresh holdout improved against the 24/51 baseline. Re-run the paired agreement figures (19/30, 1/6) as the protocol's own reliability check.
items.risk: Running k=2 per release costs about 36 agent runs, and token cost per run is unknown. Release-level numbers come from one reference book (burn is an outlier: 113 beats with no authored cast), so add a second reference book (e.g. a nonfiction one) when feasible.
items.respectsRules: Report-only. The mute test, its sample size, its bars and its prompts are unchanged; it still decides the verdict on a fresh holdout. No frame the fixes touched is used as a verdict.

items.title: 4. Cause ledger plus targeted fix rounds by cause class (no more mass re-authoring)
items.what: Add scripts/cause-ledger.js, which classifies every WRONG or dead verdict. Reuse the dossier's scratchpad classify.js taxonomy (bare-figure-no-object, generic-icon, face-mood, strike-negation, rejected-premise, twin, icon-polarity, rater-error and so on), with an owner (ENGINE/AUTHORING/VOCABULARY/RATER). It writes books/<slug>/storyboard/ledger.json and appends to a corpus ledger. A rater-error check flags judge 'why' text that contradicts its own description (6 of 46 WRONG). The runbook rule becomes: a fix round may touch only beats in a class that is AUTHORING-owned and appears in at least 2 failures, applied to every beat of that class (found by config query, not by the sample). ENGINE and VOCABULARY items go to AGENT_LOG for-review instead of being re-authored.
items.evidence: Ownership: WRONG ENGINE 46% / AUTHORING 28% / VOCABULARY 13% / RATER 13%. Rater-made: 6/46. Mass re-authoring did not help: ASN, 130 beats, dead 4→9; burn, 187 beats over two rounds, W 4→3→6. Targeted class fixes did: red-rising, 19 icons, dead 14→0; long-way-down, 8 beats in 2 classes, dead 7→0 (each delta is weak on its own given the noise).
items.expectedEffect: Beats patched per round fall from about 90-130 to tens. Fix rounds spent on engine-owned failures (about 46% of WRONG) drop to zero. Rater-error findings (13%) stop triggering edits. Expect about 3-5x less authoring rework per failing book. This does not lower misreads directly; items 2, 5 and 6 do that.
items.howWeMeasure: Beats changed per round, and rounds per book, against the baseline (burn 94+93, ASN 130). Check ledger class reliability by a second classifier pass on 50 items (agreement unknown today; the dossier split was one rater's judgement).
items.risk: The heuristic classifier misattributes owners; the dossier needed 74 manual overrides. Keep it advisory, with a human override field.
items.respectsRules: It fixes a cause class across all beats, never just the sampled beat. The verdict is still a fresh holdout. No bar changes.

items.title: 5. Negation grammar on screen: strike rendering plus a stance lint for rejected-premise callouts
items.what: (a) Engine: draw strike style so it cannot be missed and is not read backwards. Use a heavy red cross-out spanning the full phrase, the struck text desaturated, and a partial strike never ending mid-clause. Authored text and style stay identical; only how they are drawn changes. Add a strike-polarity diagnostic that warns when the struck phrase is affirmed by the narration (miracle shipped 81 inverted strikes). (b) Pre-render lint in readcheck.js or storyboard merge. It compares each callout against the narration's stance and flags callouts that state a premise the narration rejects without a strike (e.g. 'THAT ROBOT LIES'). It is report-only for the author, who decides.
items.evidence: Strike-negation is 9 of 29 WRONG outside burn (31%), the largest single non-burn class. Strike frames are WRONG 9.9% vs 4.2% (latest runs, n=81). Rejected-premise callouts are 5/29 (17%). Together, 14/29 (48%) of non-burn WRONG. Text-only readcheck found 0 WRONG on ASN before every failing run, so it does not check stance today. Pooled strike frames reach only 14-15% ADDS.
items.expectedEffect: Outside burn, if half of strike misreads and half of rejected-premise cases are caught, about 7 of 29 WRONG go away (about -24% of nonfiction WRONG, where 42 of 60 WRONG cite text). Strike WRONG could fall toward the 4.2% non-strike baseline, about a 2.3x drop for that class.
items.howWeMeasure: Run the item 3 protocol on a strike-heavy reference panel. Compare the strike-frame WRONG rate (baseline 9.9%) and the count of rejected-premise lint hits against later WRONG on new books. Track the class in the corpus ledger.
items.risk: A louder strike adds visual noise and may cost ADDS elsewhere. The stance lint uses an LLM and may over-flag; keep it advisory.
items.respectsRules: The authored text and style reach the screen unchanged, only drawn more legibly. The mute rater prompt (strike literacy) is NOT changed, because that is how the bar is computed and an operator decision.

items.title: 6. Give authors a carrier for bare-figure beats: unhide drawn icons, require own icons for named subjects, add positive icon mappings
items.what: (a) Ask the operator whether the 21 drawn but never-offered SCENE_ICONS (sword, wallet, ladder, alarmClock, work, laptopMockup, magnifier ...) can get shared-pool or world origins. They are filtered out at storyboard.js:104-107; this is a firewall-policy question. (b) Prep stop: when the bible's mustSee or the narration's top frequent nouns name a subject with no icon (ASN calendar/guilt/boundary; burn crown/god/magic/bond), require signatureObjects, so own icons get drawn and blind-named. (c) Add a positive `useFor` field to icon-readings.json rows (today 0 of 26 rows have one) and soften the storyboard.js:262-263 fallback to 'concept: null' plus a strong callout. The rule becomes: first look for a held or own object that carries the claim. The 5% cap becomes advisory, informed by measured performance.
items.evidence: bare-figure-no-object accounts for 35 of the 48 dead frames outside burn (73%); dead is 85% authoring outside burn. Frames with no icon: dead 9.4% vs 5.1%, WRONG 5.9% vs 3.4% (n=425/295); fc1 34% vs 22% dead, ADDS 38% vs 74%. Fiction own icons: WRONG 0%, dead 2.9%, ADDS 91% (n=34). ASN had 0 own icons and concept on only 25.6% of beats. Over-cap icons on burn reached ADDS 83-93%. 8 books have motifs.json, with 27 own icons in total.
items.expectedEffect: If half of the iconless beats get a valid carrier, dead outside burn falls about 25-35% (iconless dead 9.4%, carried about 5%). The dead-bar pass probability rises a lot near the threshold: P(dead≤5) is 0.60 at 17% and 0.93 at 10%. ADDS should rise toward the 60% target, since icon frames reach 74-75% vs 38-39% without. Not 10x.
items.howWeMeasure: On new books, the share of iconless beats (baseline 59%) and the dead and ADDS rates on the first fresh holdout. Run own-icons-sheet blind naming before render. Check through the cause ledger that bare-figure-no-object shrinks.
items.risk: More icons can bring back icon-polarity misreads (4 WRONG + 3 dead), because there are no broken or negated variants. Widening the firewall needs operator policy approval.
items.respectsRules: It changes vocabulary and inputs for new books, not authored decisions or bars. Published books are not touched, and authors still choose each icon.

items.title: 7. Descriptive spine act names as the HUD topic (sized by A/B before crediting it)
items.what: Story-bible validation (where spine[].act is built) requires a descriptive chapter title for each act instead of SETUP/DEVELOPMENT/TURN, since plan-antidote.js:960-965 prints ACT_AT(frame) as hud.topic on every frame. First size the effect with a report-only stills A/B on burn: same frames, generic vs descriptive HUD topic, k=2 describers.
items.evidence: LO's HUD topic took 5 descriptive values ('THE THREE DIMENSIONS OF EXPLANATORY STYLE'), and its runs were TEXT_ONLY 12/30 twice with NONE 0/60. ASN and burn printed generic act labels: NONE 9 (ASN run3) and 7 (burn run5). The authoring lens called this a confound, size unknown.
items.expectedEffect: Unknown until the A/B. At most it turns some NONE frames into TEXT_ONLY, which lowers dead and helps the dead bar, but not ADDS. Plausible upside: a few dead frames per 30 on books with generic acts. It is cheap.
items.howWeMeasure: The A/B on burn stills (dead rate with generic vs descriptive HUD). Then the first fresh holdout of new books, in the ledger, as the NONE vs TEXT_ONLY split.
items.risk: It could be read as gaming the dead bar with text. But the chapter title is real, useful on-screen information for a muted viewer, and it does not count as image ADDS, so the 'text-carried' report stays honest.
items.respectsRules: The bars and how dead is computed are unchanged. It applies to new bibles only; published books are frozen.

notDoing: Changing the 30-frame sample, the bars, the rater prompt (strike literacy or chrome preamble) or using repeat-sample verdicts. The noise math argues for it, but it is an operator-only decision under rule 2. I only flag it.
More mass re-authoring rounds. ASN: 130 beats, dead 4→9. Burn: 187 beats, W 4→3→6. 23 of 51 rounds got worse, which is indistinguishable from resampling.

Fixing the silhouette default as a priority. The 'mostly dead' claim is refuted on burn (all-silhouette frames dead 16% vs 28.5%), and the corpus evidence is n=17 from 2 books. It is a cheap cleanup at most.

Copying learned-optimism's authoring as a recipe. Its pass fits a draw at about 5% WRONG (P≈0.55) after changing 2 of 313 beats, and its dead 0 is confounded by the HUD chapter titles.
Config-based risk flags to target fix rounds. The best top third catches only 47% of WRONG (frame-risk-eval.js, 690 frames).

Framecheck as the per-book verdict, or framecheck per book. It costs 18 agents per pass and is calibrated differently from the mute test (13/90 vs 13/262 WRONG on burn). Use it for engine-release A/B only.

final.diagnosis:
Five lenses joined 720 latest-run mute frames (24 Antidote books) plus framecheck fc1 on burn-of-the-everflame (262 beats). They give 149 failure items: 46 WRONG and 119 dead. WRONG is owned 46% by ENGINE (21), 28% by AUTHORING, 13% by VOCABULARY and 13% by RATER. Dead is 64% AUTHORING and 25% ENGINE. Burn is an outlier. Cast is unauthored on 113/262 beats, so it produces nearly all of the twin, silhouette and engine-filled failures. In the other 23 books dead is 85% authoring, and bare-figure-no-object accounts for 35/48 of it. 59% of frames carry no icon. Those frames are dead 9.4% (vs 5.1% with an icon) and WRONG 5.9% (vs 3.4%), and they ADD 39% vs 75%.

The largest WRONG classes are drawn by the engine or created by how negation is shown:
- Beard and stubble form a U under the mouth. Faces with a beard read 'smiling' 21.8% of the time vs 6.6% without (n=354/1,341). An unintended smile carries WRONG 21.2% vs 9.0%, and this is about 28% of fiction WRONG.
- The neutral mouth v1 is a U-curve and is still the default. Verified at Everyman.tsx:61, NEUTRAL_MOUTH_VERSION="v1".
- The authorship lock seals the engine's twin cast whenever art.json sets only `set`. Verified at plan-antidote.js:1183-1186. 20 locked twin beats; in fc1 the twoShot frames are 6/6 dead.
- The `game` icon is a trophy cup: 3/3 WRONG, used in 44 scenes. It also runs a perpetual Math.sin shine at motifs.tsx:806-817, which breaks the no-idle-oscillation rule.
- Strike and rejected-premise callouts are 14/29 (48%) of non-burn WRONG. Strike frames are WRONG 9.9% vs 4.2%.

The measuring instrument is noisy, and most of that noise comes from the describer. Re-describing a frame gives WRONG kappa 0.03-0.27; re-judging the same description agrees 92%. On 30 frames, P(WRONG<=1) is 0.88 at a true 2% rate and 0.55 at 5%. P(dead<=5) is 0.17 at burn's 26%. That is why 23 of 51 fix rounds got worse, why 57% of mute runs (46/81) went to books that never passed, and why learned-optimism's pass (2 of 313 beats changed) was close to a coin flip. Readcheck catches only 7/54 mute WRONG.

The data substrate is at risk. Verified: audit/ in the main checkout has no mute/ or framecheck/ folder. The only copy is the untracked tree of stash@{0} (6,146 mute files and 557 framecheck files).

Where 10x is real and where it is not:
- Inside single classes: twins, game, beard grin about 3x.
- In wasted effort: fix rounds, re-authoring, re-samples.
- Whole-film WRONG and dead: an honest expectation is about 1.5-2.5x, because dead is mostly authoring and about 13% of WRONG is rater error.

items.title: 4. Fix-round protocol: owner routing, class-wide fixes, no re-sampling an unchanged film
items.what: Codify in STORYBOARD_RUNBOOK.md (§3b/§5) and the preview-hazirla skill. (1) Classify every WRONG/dead finding by owner: ENGINE, VOCABULARY, AUTHORING, RATER. Start with a scripts/cause-ledger.js built from the dossier taxonomy, advisory, with a manual-override field. (2) ENGINE and VOCABULARY findings go to AGENT_LOG for-review, never into the storyboard. (3) An AUTHORING fix touches a class only when it is confirmed: seen in >=2 failures, or found by 2 agreeing describer passes, or confirmed by the author opening the still. The fix is applied to every beat of that class, found with similar-candidates.js, not to the sampled beat. Report the beat count (soft cap ~25, waivable with a reason). (4) No new fresh holdout on a film that has not changed since the last one. (5) Flag judge 'why' lines that contradict their own description as RATER. The verdict stays one fresh mute holdout with unchanged bars.
items.evidence: 51 run transitions: 24 better, 23 worse, 7 flat. Mass rounds: burn 94+93 beats, W 4->3->6; ASN 130 beats, dead 4->9. Small class fixes: red-rising 19 icons dead 14->0, long-way-down 8 beats dead 7->0 (each weak alone). Describer kappa for WRONG 0.03-0.27; fc1 vs run5 shared 1 of 8 WRONG flags. 6/46 WRONG are rater-made. 21-days: re-sampled 7 minutes apart, W7 -> W1.
items.expectedEffect: Beats patched per round: ~90-130 -> ~10-25. No rounds spent on engine-owned (46% of WRONG) or rater (13%) failures. This is the realistic 10x, on wasted effort, not on misreads.
items.howWeMeasure: Per new book in AGENT_LOG: beats changed per round, mute runs to PASS or operator decision (baseline 2.70 runs, 9/30 first-pass), and the sign of change between runs (baseline 24/51 improved). A second classifier pass on 50 ledger items gives the ledger's reliability.
items.risk: Classifier misattributes owners (the dossier needed 74 manual overrides), so it stays advisory. The 'unchanged film' rule is a process rule; put it to the operator in one line, because it touches how often the verdict is drawn but not how it is computed.

items.title: 5. Negation grammar: legible strike rendering + advisory stance lint
items.what: (a) Renderer, authored words and style unchanged: a strike drawn across the whole phrase, heavy and unmistakable at small scale, with the struck words dimmed. No added glyphs or stamps (a red NO/X would decorate an authored beat). (b) Merge lint in storyboard.js, report-only with a per-beat waive reason. It flags: a strike with no unstruck companion; a partial strike inside a clause; a callout whose tokens sit inside a negation scope in the narration window (not/never/isn't/rather than/myth), i.e. a rejected premise stated alone; and a strike on a phrase the narration affirms (polarity). (c) Rules.md: when the narration rejects X, show 'NOT X -> Y' or Y alone, never X alone. (d) Keep the verbatim-strike rule at visual-strategy.js:68/282 as it is, but report every demotion visibly instead of dropping it silently. Loosening it needs blind evidence first.
items.files: src/engines/antidote (callout/strike renderer), scripts/storyboard.js (merge lint + rules text), scripts/lib/visual-strategy.js (report demotions), data/icon-readings.json (strike rows)

Creativity lost 47 authored strikes to silent demotion.

items.title: 6. Replace the bare-figure fallback with a required visual carrier (report-only lint)

The fallback 'concept: null + stage the PEOPLE + strong callout' becomes: name a carrier, which is an own icon, a shared icon whose `useFor` fits, a held signature object, a diagram, or a physical action from the measured-readable set. items.title: 9. Component-sheet harness as the engine acceptance step
items.what: scripts/component-sheet.js renders face, pose, icon, state and strike sheets headlessly (the same path as own-icons-sheet.js), runs k=3-4 fresh blind sonnet describers one image at a time, and writes rows to data/icon-readings.json with a per-component history. It is required on any rig, icon or text-render change. Report-only; never the preview verdict.
items.evidence: The beard grin was found only after several failed mute runs on several books. own-icons-sheet caught casserole->toaster and hook->noose in seconds. Describer noise dominates, which is why k>=3 is needed.

items.howWeMeasure: Per new book: count face, pose and icon misreads first found on a sheet vs first found in mute or framecheck (logged in AGENT_LOG).
items.risk: Sheets show components without context (crops, timing, narration contrast), so book-level framecheck stays the integration check. Agent cost per run is unknown.

items.title: 10. Release-level report-only framecheck with 2 describer passes on 2 reference books
items.what: framecheck.js `--passes=2`: a fresh describer per chunk per pass, one judge per description. It stores tallies per class with binomial CIs and per-frame findings only where both passes agree. Run once per engine release on burn (parked) AND one not-yet-published non-fiction book, because burn alone is an outlier. First run an anchor test on run5's 30 stills through both pipelines to resolve the gap between mute runs (13/90 WRONG) and fc1 (13/262).
items.evidence: Measurement lens: ±2 points needs every beat x ~4 passes. k=2 rater sd ~1.5 points, so k=2 can resolve class-level shifts (smile-read rate, twin count), not 1-point WRONG shifts. Calibration gap McNemar p~0.06.
items.expectedEffect: Gives engine A/B numbers that are not a 30-frame lottery. It measures, and does not by itself improve fidelity.
items.howWeMeasure: Self-reliability: the paired agreement (baseline 19/30, 1/6 WRONG) re-measured on each release.
items.risk: ~36 agent runs per release; token cost unknown (no cost ledger).

items.title: 11. Readable bodies: fix 'think' and 'slump', then two-body relational verbs

Both must pass a blind pose sheet. Later, and only if Tier 2 still leaves fiction dead high: two-body verbs (embrace, confront, kneel-before, hand-over, protect) with paired twoShot slot geometry.

items.howWeMeasure: A pose sheet with each verb named in >=2/3 blind reads before it enters rules.md. On new fiction books, framecheck dead for action vs idle frames.

final.validationPlan:
Baseline first (Tier 1 item 0): restore the corpus and freeze the reference numbers.
- 720 latest-run frames: WRONG 4.9%, dead 7.6%.
- No-icon vs icon frames: dead 9.4% vs 5.1%.
- Strike vs non-strike frames: WRONG 9.9% vs 4.2%.
- Beard vs no beard, read 'smiling': 21.8% vs 6.6%.
- burn fc1: WRONG 13/262, dead 68/262; 6 twin frames.

(1) Component level, before any book. Run the blind sheets (faces x beard x blink, game icon, strikes, poses, icon states) with fresh sonnet describers, one image at a time, k>=3. Each sheet must first reproduce the old misread on the old drawing; that shows the sheet can detect the defect. Then it must show the new drawing does not misread. The rows go into data/icon-readings.json.

(2) Engine A/B on burn-of-the-everflame, which is parked and not published, so re-planning it is allowed.
- Re-plan from the same art.json, and render the same 262 beats at the same sample moments.
- Run report-only framecheck with 2 describer passes.
- Primary endpoints are the CLASS rates k=2 can resolve: smile-reads on configured-neutral faces, the twin-frame count (must be 0), game/trophy misreads, and lock.cast set without authored cast (must be 0).
- Whole-film WRONG and dead are reported with CIs and not over-claimed, because k=2 cannot resolve 1-point changes.
- Burn is an outlier (113 unauthored-cast beats). Before generalising, add an anchor test, re-describing run5's 30 stills through both pipelines, to settle the mute vs framecheck calibration gap.

(3) The verdict is always the next NEW book. Its first fresh mute holdout is drawn once, with unchanged bars, the unchanged rater prompt and 30 frames. No frame touched by a fix is ever the verdict. A film is not re-sampled until it has changed.

(4) Program success is judged over the next 3 new Antidote books against the 30-book process baseline (2.70 mute runs per book, 9/30 first-pass, 23/51 rounds getting worse), using:
- runs per book;
- beats changed per round;
- the share of findings routed to ENGINE/VOCABULARY/RATER rather than re-authored;
- the CARRIERLESS share;
- the strike-frame WRONG rate;
- the neutral smile-read rate.

Given the binomial noise (P(pass) 0.55 at a true 5% WRONG rate), a single pass or fail is never treated as proof. Effects are only credited when the class rates move in the predicted direction across books.
notDoing: Changing the 30-frame sample size, the bars, verdicting on repeated samples, or adding strike literacy or a chrome preamble to the mute rater prompt. The noise math argues for it (a 30-frame run cannot separate 2% WRONG from 5%), but how the bar is computed is the operator's decision. Flagged, not done.
More mass re-authoring rounds. ASN's 130 beats took dead from 4 to 9; burn's 187 beats moved WRONG 4->3->6; 23 of 51 rounds got worse.
Flipping the illustration/diorama silhouette default now. In burn fc1, silhouette frames are LESS often dead (16% vs 29%), and the contrary corpus sample is n=17 from 2 books.
Adding a red NO stamp or X glyph to authored strikes. It would decorate an authored beat (invariant 1). Only the strike line itself is drawn heavier.
Dropping the verbatim-strike demotion without blind evidence that non-verbatim strikes read correctly. Demotions are reported instead.
Making prep hard-refuse until gap icons are drawn. A strong warning with a recorded waive is used instead; the threshold is untested and the own-icon gain rests on n=34.
Treating text-only readcheck as a predictor or a gate investment. It caught 7/54 mute WRONG, and 0 on ASN before 3 failing runs.
Targeting fix rounds with config risk flags. The best top third catches only 47% of WRONG.
Copying learned-optimism's authoring as a recipe. Its pass fits a coin flip at a pooled 5% WRONG after changing 2 of 313 beats, and is confounded by the HUD chapter titles.
Framecheck per book or as a verdict. It costs 18 agents per pass and its calibration against the mute test is unresolved (13/90 vs 13/262).
Firewall REVIEW triage sessions. 6 of the 7 blocked books shipped anyway, and the policy is already noBlock.
Engine auto-insertion of icons or broken states on authored beats to fill bare figures. Invariant 1 forbids it.
Retrofitting any published book (flowers silhouettes, beloved twins, a-good-man unauthored cast). They are frozen; old configs only need to keep rendering.
